title: Role Training, Qualification and Competency Evidence

content.overview: Professional training should match the risk and complexity of the task. Reading a document can demonstrate exposure to information; it does not by itself demonstrate that a person can perform a critical procedure correctly.

vocabulary.definition: Evidence that assigned learning or instruction was completed.
Documented evidence that a person meets defined requirements to perform a role or task.
Observation or assessment of actual task execution against defined criteria.

sections.title: Match evidence to the learning outcome
sections.body: Knowledge outcomes can be assessed with questions; performance-critical tasks may require observed demonstration or supervised execution.

sections.title: Train to the current version
sections.body: When controlled procedures change materially, affected roles need impact review and retraining before the new method becomes routine.

sections.title: Do not overclaim credentials
sections.body: ASTM distinguishes certificate programs from personnel certification. THC Academy training should describe what was actually taught and assessed rather than implying a license or external certification.

workedExamples: A worker can pass a sanitation quiz yet still require observed demonstration before independently executing a sterile transfer process.
An editorial typo may not require retraining, while a changed disinfectant sequence may.
commonMistakes: Keeping training records with no procedure version.
Calling internal training a government certification.
content.practicalApplication: For each SOP role, classify outcomes as know, interpret or perform; assign a matching training/assessment method and record the SOP version used.
content.summary: Professional training becomes defensible when its evidence matches what the role must actually know or perform.
